researched_writeups.title: New Oriental Education (EDU) - East Asia Stock Insights
researched_writeups.summary: The memo uses a Sum-Of-The-Parts (SOTP) framework to value EDU at $150 per share (100%+ upside), applying a 50% holdco discount to its 57% stake in public live-stream ecommerce arm East Buy ($0.4B) while valuing core education at $24.8B via DCF. Key operational catalysts include non-academic youth tutoring EBIT margins expanding to 22%, high school tutoring margins reaching 24% through Online-Merge-Offline (OMO) capacity utilization, and a projected 30% CAGR in earnings ex-East Buy.

researched_writeups.title: What do y'all think about EDU (New Oriental)
researched_writeups.summary: The pitch presents a classic sum-of-the-parts deep value thesis, highlighting $3.0B in net cash after debt and a $2.0B market value for EDU's 57% controlling stake in East Buy. This effectively prices EDU's core cash-generating tutoring and study-abroad consultancy business at an enterprise value of ~$3.35B against $600M in TTM free cash flow (~5.6x FCF). Key catalysts include rapid post-restructuring top-line revenue growth and leverage of EDU's strong institutional brand moat in non-academic learning.

researched_writeups.title: Top Performing China Stocks of 2023
researched_writeups.summary: The research write-up documents EDU's turnaround strategy following the Chinese government's 2021 Double Reduction crackdown on primary school tutoring. The analysis focuses on unit economics recovery driven by pivoting core operations toward adult test prep, vocational exams, and non-academic youth courses, alongside monetizing bilingual teaching talent via live-stream e-commerce platform East Buy. Catalyst-driven earnings restoration and high ROE execution drove the stock's multi-fold re-rating from trough levels.

researched_writeups.title: $EDU: say what you will about Chinese stocks, but $EDU has no business trading at NEGATIVE $600m EV
researched_writeups.summary: Written during peak sector panic following China's crackdown on K-9 tutoring, this DD highlights a severe net-net / negative enterprise value dislocation where EDU held $4.0B in net cash against a $3.4B market capitalization, valuing its remaining legal $1.0B revenue segments at -$600M EV. Drawing parallels to negative-EV turnarounds like Luckin Coffee, the write-up targets an immediate base-case re-rating to $3.50+ per share (~50-60%+ upside) based purely on net cash backing and residual study-abroad cash flows.
